name: East Asian Lang Cultures (PhD)

rules.name: Program Requirements
rules.desc: Complete the following requirements by the end of Year 2 of study.

children.name: Proseminar Sequence Requirement (EALC 201)
children.desc: Complete two proseminar courses, EALC 201 in the first year of study and an additional course as associated with the student's subplan. EALC 202 is required for all literature students, CHINA 290 is required for all Chinese linguistics students, and JAPAN 279 is required for all Japanese linguistics students. Students in Chinese archaeology must take an advisor-approved course with subject code CHINA, ARCHLGY, or ANTHRO.

children.name: Additional Advisor-Approved Six Courses Requirement
children.desc: Complete six advisor-approved courses in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and/or trans-Asian literature, culture, linguistics, anthropology, archaeology, art and art history, history, philosophy, political science, religious studies, sociology, or another field, as approved by the student’s advisor, not including courses taken to fulfill the proseminar or language requirements.

Submit a full draft of the student's qualifying paper to the primary advisor by May 15 of Spring Quarter and the final version by the last Friday of May. Students are also required to present qualifying paper research at the last meeting of the East Asian Humanities and East Asian Linguistics workshops (the joint student symposium) at the end of Spring Quarter.
children.name: Qualifying paper and symposium presentation

rules.name: Teaching Experience Requirement
rules.desc: Teaching is core to the academic and professional training of doctoral students in East Asian Languages and Cultures. All students are required to complete three quarters of teaching experiences by Spring Quarter of Year 4 regardless of their financial support. Most students are typically expected to complete more than the required number of teaching experiences, which may be in an East Asian language or cultural content courses as approved by the advisor, as part of their professional training. In rare cases, the department may approve exceptions to the timing and changes to the type(s) of course(s) used in fulfillment of the teaching requirement.

children.name: East Asian Literatures and/or Linguistics Teaching Requirement
Preparatory Teaching Course
children.desc: Complete the following course during Spring Quarter of the year prior to serving as a teaching assistant. Typically, this occurs during Spring Quarter of the Year 2.
children.notes: Before enrolling in DLCL 301, graduate students should have attained an Intermediate-High level of oral proficiency on the ACTFL/FSI scale in the foreign language they intend to teach.

children.name: Teaching Experience Requirement
children.desc: Students in East Asian Literatures or Linguistics are expected to fulfill the three-quarter teaching experience requirement through an East Asian language course sequence.

children.name: Chinese Archaeology Teaching Requirement
children.desc: Students in Chinese Archaeology are expected to fulfill the required three quarters of teaching experiences through East Asian archaeology courses or other courses as approved by the advisor. Students must have successfully completed the course prior to starting the teaching experience.

rules.name: Advancement to Candidacy
rules.desc: Admission to candidacy is a prospective judgement by the faculty of a student’s potential to successfully complete the requirements of the degree program. Students are expected to complete qualifying procedures and apply for candidacy by the end of Year 2. Qualifying procedures in the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures (EALC) include completion of the required coursework associated with the program requirements in the relevant subplan area and submission of a qualifying paper (equivalent to an M.A. thesis up to 30 pages in length, with the first draft submitted to the advisor by May 15 and final draft by the last Friday of May) and presentation of qualifying paper research (at the last meeting of the East Asian Humanities and East Asian Linguistics workshops during the student symposium at the end of Spring Quarter of Year 2). EALC faculty vote on each second year student's admission to candidacy during a meeting held in the first week of June. Additional details on qualifying procedures can be found in the EALC Graduate Handbook.

rules.name: Oral Exam
rules.desc: In the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures, the oral exam is a defense of the dissertation presented upon completion of a pre-final draft submitted to reading committee members at least three weeks prior to the defense date. Students consult with their dissertation advisor and reading committee members on the timing of the defense at the beginning of the intended submission quarter of the dissertation. The date of dissertation defense should be set at least a month in advance, and must take place at least two weeks prior to the filing deadline to allow for ample time for any revisions that the reading committee deem necessary for the filing. Students are expected to complete this milestone by the end of the fifth year of study.

rules.name: Dissertation
rules.desc: Students are required to submit an approved dissertation in English (approval for writing the dissertation in another language is normally granted only in cases where the other language or literature in that language is also the subject of the discipline, and such dissertations written in another language must include an extended summary in English) that makes an original contribution to the field of East Asian languages and cultures in final form as approved by the reading committee at least two weeks prior to the final manuscript submission deadline to the final reader (and additional committee members as necessary). Students are expected to submit the dissertation in the same quarter that they complete the oral exam, and no later than the subsequent quarter.

rules.name: Language Proficiency Requirement
rules.desc: Demonstrate proficiency in at least two research languages chosen and at a level approved by the primary advisor according to the student's specific research goals. Students must be proficient at the fourth-year level at the minimum in the primary research language and at the second-year level at the minimum in the secondary research language; higher levels of proficiency may be required depending on the advisor’s recommendation. Proficiency must be certified through examination and/or coursework through the Stanford Language Center and to be determined on a case-by-case basis. When deemed necessary by the student’s advisor(s), working knowledge of a third language may also be required.

children.name: Comprehensive Qualifying Examination Requirement
children.desc: The comprehensive examination is a two-hour oral exam on Japanese literature with three examiners. The reading list (maximum 150 titles) must be approved by them at least one quarter in advance. The list must include primary texts in Japanese literature as well as core texts in methodology; students may also add a subfield and a fourth examiner if deemed necessary by their primary advisor for their research and credentialing. To pass the exam, students must demonstrate competency in literary history and critical issues for the field of Japanese literary studies, selected methodologies, and key issues in any subfield. The comprehensive exam must be completed by the end of the fourth year.

children.desc: Submit two qualifying papers (QPs) that present the student’s original research in two different subfields of linguistics discussing Japanese linguistic topics and data of acceptable quality for presentation at a professional conference and/or publishing in a linguistics journal. Each QP must be about 25-30 pages, may be an extension of a term paper, and are to be evaluated by a faculty committee, with topics and committee members decided with approval by the primary faculty advisor. The first qualifying paper (QP1) should be submitted as a draft to the committee in winter quarter of the second year, with the final draft to be submitted by week 5 of spring quarter of the second year. The second qualifying paper (QP2) should be submitted to the committee as a draft by the end of spring quarter of the third year, with the final draft to be submitted by the beginning of the fourth year.

gpa: Students are expected to earn an overall GPA of 3.0 or better across all courses.
grading: Students must take all required courses for a letter grade when this option is available, and receive a grade of B+ or better in all required coursework.
transferPolicy: The EALC Department accepts residency transfer credit. Refer to the University policy on Graduate Transfer Credit. Students must receive the approval of their primary faculty advisor for any course substitutions or petitions of changes to the fulfillment of degree requirements.
reviewNotes: You choose one track in your subplan: four in East Asian Literatures (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Trans-Asian), two in East Asian Linguistics (Chinese, Japanese), or the Chinese Archaeology subplan with its research courses and second proseminar. Everyone takes EALC 201, EALC 299 for the qualifying paper, DLCL 301 or the archaeology teaching path, the language proficiency courses for their language, and the track's courses; the program-wide proseminar, six-course and language rules count the same courses the track lists. Every required course must be taken for a letter grade when one is offered and passed with a B+ or better, and the degree needs 135 units. Non-heritage Chinese proficiency can be met with CHINLANG 225 and 251 or a semester abroad taught in Chinese. Thesis, dissertation research, practicum and TGR enrollments count toward the 135 units but never as seminars or field courses. Advisor-approved courses are counted by subject, level and number; you confirm by hand your advisor's approval of them, the supporting language, the comprehensive exams, qualifying papers, prospectus, teaching, candidacy, oral exam, dissertation and the 3.0 GPA.
